title: SHAD Canada
cost: ~$2,400 CAD program fee (need-based financial aid and full bursaries available)
description: A month-long summer enrichment program hosted at Canadian universities where students tackle entrepreneurial STEM design challenges. Highly regarded by Canadian universities as a marker of academic excellence and initiative.

title: Canada-Wide Science Fair
description: The pinnacle science fair in Canada where students present independent research projects to expert judges after qualifying through regional fairs. Offers scholarships and recognition valued by science and engineering faculties.

title: FIRST Robotics Competition
organization: FIRST (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology)
description: Students design, build, and program industrial-size robots to compete in alliance-based matches. Builds engineering, teamwork, and project-management skills prized by engineering programs worldwide.

title: HOSA - Future Health Professionals
cost: ~$25–$40 CAD annual membership, plus competition/conference fees
description: A career and technical student organization for students interested in health sciences, offering competitive events, leadership roles, and healthcare-focused learning. Valuable for students pursuing pre-med or health science pathways.
verificationNote: Confirm current chapter/registration process directly with HOSA Ontario before relying on this — provincial HOSA chapter structures can change year to year.

title: Canadian Business Ethics Case Competition
organization: Various Canadian universities (hosted on a rotating basis)
description: High school teams analyze real-world business ethics dilemmas and present solutions to judges from academia and industry. Sharpens critical thinking and persuasive presentation skills for business applicants.
verificationNote: I could not confirm a currently-active, standing 'Canadian Business Ethics Case Competition' at the high school level under this exact name — the Rotman link is a general faculty homepage, not a program page. Recommend verifying this listing exists and finding its actual event page before publishing, or replacing it.

title: DECA Ontario
cost: ~$40–$60 CAD membership + conference/competition fees (often $100+ for regional/provincial events)
description: Students compete in case-study and roleplay events covering marketing, finance, hospitality, and entrepreneurship. Develops business acumen and public speaking skills highly relevant for business school applications.

title: JA Company Program
description: Students launch and run a real micro-business over the school year, learning finance, marketing, and operations from volunteer mentors. Provides hands-on entrepreneurial experience for business-minded students.

title: National Economics Challenge
description: A quiz-style competition testing microeconomics, macroeconomics, and current events, culminating in a national championship. Highly respected by economics and business programs.
verificationNote: This is a U.S. competition (Council for Economic Education is American). Ontario students can sometimes participate, but confirm eligibility before including it as a Canadian-focused option.

title: Wall Street Survivor Investment Trading Challenge
description: Students manage a simulated stock portfolio using real market data to compete for the best investment returns. Builds financial literacy and market analysis skills for finance-track applicants.
verificationNote: Removed the TMX/Toronto Stock Exchange co-attribution — I could not confirm TMX currently co-runs a 'Knowledge Bowl' with Wall Street Survivor; this looks like it may have conflated two separate programs. TMX does run its own investor education initiatives, which may be a better link — worth checking tmx.com directly.

title: Model United Nations (Ontario circuit, e.g. TDSBMUN)
organization: Various university and school-hosted MUN conferences
cost: $20–$100+ CAD per conference (delegate fee), varies by conference
description: Students role-play as diplomats debating global issues in simulated UN committees, honing negotiation, research, and public speaking skills. Widely respected as evidence of leadership and global awareness.
verificationNote: The original link (una.org.uk) is the UK's national UN association, not an Ontario-specific resource — kept as general background on 'what is MUN' but you'll want to swap in a specific conference's page (e.g. a TDSBMUN or NAIMUN registration page) once you pick one, since these run on their own sites and change yearly.

title: Shad Valley Entrepreneurship Program
cost: ~$2,400 CAD program fee (need-based financial aid and full bursaries available)
description: An extension of the SHAD program focused on entrepreneurial leadership, pitching business ideas to real judges. Combines innovation and leadership development highly valued in top-tier applications.
verificationNote: This appears to duplicate entry #3 (SHAD Canada) — SHAD's program is a single unified program rather than having a separately-branded 'Shad Valley Entrepreneurship' track today. Consider merging these two entries.

title: Student Trustee / School Board Representative
description: Elected students represent the student body at official school board meetings, voicing concerns and shaping policy. A high-visibility leadership role recognized by Ontario universities.
verificationNote: This is applied for through your own school board (not a single national body) — direct students to their local school board's website for the actual application process.

title: Canadian Red Cross Youth Program
description: Replaces the discontinued 'Free the Children / WE Schools' entry (WE Charity wound down its Canadian school operations in September 2020 and no longer runs active school programming). The Canadian Red Cross Youth program offers structured volunteering, disaster-response training, and community campaigns for high school students, and is a currently active, well-recognized alternative for social-action-focused volunteer experience.

title: Duke of Edinburgh's International Award
organization: The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award – Canada
cost: Approx. $110–$130 CAD registration fee per level (Bronze/Silver/Gold), plus optional equipment/expedition costs
description: A globally recognized self-development framework combining volunteering, physical activity, skill-building, and an expedition. Bronze, Silver, and Gold levels are recognized internationally as evidence of well-rounded character.

title: Habitat for Humanity Youth Program
description: Students volunteer on home-building projects and fundraising initiatives supporting affordable housing in their communities. Provides tangible, hands-on service experience with a well-known international organization.

title: Ontario Youth Volunteer Challenge
description: Students engage in structured community service projects that count toward Ontario's mandatory 40 volunteer hours while building civic engagement. Demonstrates sustained community commitment to admissions committees.
verificationNote: I could not confirm a specific, currently-active program called the 'Ontario Youth Volunteer Challenge.' The URL provided is Ontario's general community-involvement graduation requirement page, not a distinct program. Recommend either verifying this program name and finding a real program page, or reframing this entry simply as 'Ontario's 40-Hour Community Involvement Requirement.'

title: Canadian Improv Games
cost: Team registration fee, Varies by Year
description: A national high school improv theatre competition where teams perform unscripted scenes judged on creativity and teamwork. Builds confidence, collaboration, and performance skills for arts-focused applicants.

title: Canadian Student Debating Federation Nationals
description: The national championship for competitive high school debate, testing rhetorical skill, argumentation, and critical thinking. A prestigious credential demonstrating communication ability across disciplines.

title: Kiwanis Music Festival
organization: Federation of Canadian Music Festivals / Local Kiwanis Clubs
cost: $20–$50 CAD per class/entry, varies by local festival
description: A long-running regional music competition where students perform solo or ensemble pieces before adjudicators for feedback and awards. A respected credential for students pursuing music conservatory or arts programs.
verificationNote: Kiwanis Music Festivals are run locally by city (e.g. Kiwanis Music Festival of Greater Toronto), not one national site — confirm the correct local festival URL for your area.

title: Ontario Arts Council Youth & Community Arts Programs
cost: Free to apply (grants program, not an entry-fee competition)
description: The Ontario Arts Council mainly funds artists, organizations, and projects through grants rather than running a single youth art 'competition' — students are more likely to encounter it via school- or organization-led grant-funded exhibitions than as a direct entry competition.
verificationNote: Renamed from 'Ontario Provincial Art Competitions' — I could not confirm a program specifically named 'Ontario Youth Arts' currently run by the Ontario Arts Council. If a student is looking for an actual student art competition, consider Ontario Society of Artists' student exhibitions or a school board art show instead.

title: TIFF Next Wave Committee
description: Students join a youth advisory committee that programs and promotes a film festival for teens, gaining exposure to the film industry. Offers unique arts-administration and event-organizing experience.
verificationNote: Confirm the committee is currently recruiting when a student applies — TIFF youth programs periodically pause or restructure between seasons.

title: Canadian Computing Competition (CCC)
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A programming contest testing algorithmic problem-solving in any language, used by top computer science programs to identify talented applicants. Top scorers may qualify for the Canadian Computing Olympiad.

title: Canadian Senior Mathematics Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A national math contest testing curriculum-based problem solving for senior high school students. Participation and awards strengthen STEM applications and demonstrate quantitative reasoning ability.

title: Euclid Mathematics Contest
organization: Centre for Education in Mathematics and Computing (CEMC), University of Waterloo
description: A challenging math contest for senior students that is widely used by Waterloo and other universities for scholarship and admission consideration. Strong results demonstrate advanced problem-solving skills valued in engineering and math programs.
